issues.description: Terminal states all have the same rank, so an older FAILED/CANCELLED/COMPLETED snapshot can overwrite a newer terminal record.
The unchanged check ignores user, partition, submit/start, alloc_cpus, gpus, and exit_code, leaving corrected accounting fields stale.
Using only job_id as the primary key risks overwriting historical jobs when Slurm job IDs are reused or multiple clusters are ingested.
Timezone-aware timestamps are stored and compared as strings, which can include or exclude the wrong jobs chronologically.
Database files are created with default process permissions, which can expose user/job accounting data on shared systems.
Required logical fields such as user, partition, submit, and exit_code are accepted as empty strings or null reference times.
Usage and top-user reports include pending/running records, so queued jobs can appear in usage rankings with zero consumed resources.
The jobs table has no indexes on reference time, user, partition, or state, so reports will full-scan as the database grows.
Project metadata defines pytest only and lacks linting, formatting, type checking, or coverage gates for ongoing development.
